text:
sara: FYI I flipped the opportunistic-buffer-lending feature on the canary cluster at 10:02 UTC to test cross-pool lending of logits <-> kv scratchpads. Expected: lower steady GPU mem and fewer large alloc spikes. Results are mixed so far.

kai: I see 3 OOM incidents in the canary job since the change. stack shows `cudaMalloc` failures inside tensor_pool::acquire.

andrew: can you paste the allocation trace for one of the OOMs? want to see ordering of frees/lends.

sara: pasted one trace below (trimmed). this was from the canary pod id=canary-42 at 10:10:12 UTC:
```
alloc 0x7f9a2c000 size=12_582_912 logits_buf (slot L1)
alloc 0x7f9a3d000 size=8_388_608 activation_buf (slot A3)
lend slot L1 -> kv_scratch (borrower id=shard-7, seq_len=1024)
alloc fail: cudaMalloc 0x0 size=24_000_000 (requested for next_logits)
attempted free slot A3 -> deferred (in-flight borrower)
OOM
```

kai: two things stick out: the borrower had seq_len=1024 and held the logits slot across multiple steps; lending policy assumed short borrow windows but this one was long. also the allocator didn't preemptively shrink inactive slabs to satisfy the new allocation.

vasu: interesting — our lending heuristic assumed borrower lifetime < 8ms. large seq_len workloads break that. we should add a lifetime cap and a size cap per buffer type.

andrew: +1. also kernel selection changes last week increased peak temp workspace for some transformer kernels (fused attention -> workspace +15%). combined effect could push us over. can we correlate deploys?

perf-bot: anomaly detected: canary cluster opportunistic-lending ON -> 3 OOMs in 2h, p95 latency +6%, p99 latency +9%. Change flagged for investigation.

sara: i verified the kernel change rolled at 09:58 UTC. so lending + kernel workspace bump likely interactive. current hypothesis: lending steals logits buffers that would have been reused for high-workspace kernels, causing cudaMalloc to spike.

kai: quick mitigation options:
- disable opportunistic lending for logits buffers entirely (safe, perf downside)
- add heuristic: forbid lending when estimated workspace_headroom < buffer_size * 1.5
- cap lending duration: max_lend_ms = 10ms and force immediate reclaim path if exceeded

vasu: i like the headroom heuristic. it's cheap: when considering lending, compute projected_workspace = active_workspace + worst_kernel_workspace_for_model(model_id) and only lend if projected_workspace + borrower_request <= gpu_capacity * 0.95.

andrew: we can get worst_kernel_workspace from our kernel-profile table (we log per-model per-kernel workspace). fallback to conservative constant if unknown.

sara: prototype patch: added `lend_guard` check and `max_lend_ms` timer. diff excerpt:
```cpp
bool can_lend(BufferSlot s, Borrower b) {
  if (s.type == LOGITS && borrower.seq_len > 512) return false;
  if (projected_workspace_for_model(b.model) + s.size > gpu_headroom_threshold) return false;
  return true;
}

// in borrower path
start_lend_timer(ms=10);
if (lend_timer.expired()) trigger_reclaim(s);
```

kai: can we test with a stress harness that simulates mix of seq_len 32/128/1024 and kernels with +15% workspace? i can modify the loadgen.

sara: starting stress run now on canary with `max_lend_ms=10` and headroom heuristic enabled. will report back after 15m.

perf-bot: stress run started: canary/loadgen-092 -> 12k requests, mix {32:60%,128:30%,1024:10%}.

andrew: separate note — the allocator's delayed-free list keeps ~2x buffer count for safety; we should consider aggressive immediate free when lending is enabled to avoid double reservation. that might reduce peak. but need to measure fragmentation impact.

kai: agree — maybe a mode `immediate_free_on_lend` that bypasses delayed-free and returns memory to CUDA as soon as borrower releases. risk: thrashing if allocations oscillate.

sara: stress run update after 12m: 6k requests processed, no new OOMs so far, p95 latency slightly up (+2%) but overall memory footprint reduced ~12% compared to baseline without lending.

vasu: promising. can you fetch a sample allocation timeline showing lend/reclaim events? want to validate reclaim path is fast enough.

sara: pasted sample timeline (truncated):
```
[10:28:05] allocate logits L1 -> slot A
[10:28:05] lend L1 -> shard-7 (seq=1024) -> start_timer
[10:28:05] kernel workspace reserve -> +18MB (fused-attn)
[10:28:05] borrower returns L1 after 9ms -> reclaim success
[10:28:06] allocate next_logits -> reuse L1 -> success
```

kai: reclaim in 9ms looks ok for these runs. problem cases are when borrower holds > max_lend_ms or when multiple borrowers gang up on the same slot type causing headroom exhaustion. headroom heuristic should block lending in those scenarios.

andrew: next steps:
- run a 1h canary with synthetic extreme seq_len traffic to ensure no edge OOMs (and collect perf metrics)
- if stable, roll to staging for broader kernel/workload mix
- otherwise rollback opportunistic lending for logits and keep for activations/scratchpads only

sara: logging followups: add two extra metrics `lend_duration_ms` histogram and `lend_blocked_by_headroom_count`. that will help triage in the future.

perf-bot: stress run progress: 30% complete, no OOMs observed, p99 latency trend flat.

vasu: if after 1h it's stable, let's accept the heuristic but keep `opportunistic_lending_ratio` defaulted to 0.25 and expose config per-customer (some customers have large seq_len workloads).

kai: can we also add a quick circuit breaker: if OOM_count_in_5m >= 1 then auto-disable lending for logits for that node? cheap safety valve.

sara: added circuit-breaker to the branch. will watch the canary. thanks all — good triage. follow-up: @andrew can you own the 1h run and collect kernel profile correlation data? @kai add the loadgen scenarios for extreme seq_len. i'll file a tiny RFC for the heuristics/flags and link after the run. :thumbsup:

andrew: on it.

kai: writing loadgen patch now.

perf-bot: canary run completed (1h): processed 72k requests, 0 OOMs, p95 +1.8%, p99 +2.1%, gpu mem mean -10%. tagging patch as `opportunistic-lending:v2` for rollout consideration.
